# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

User Guide

RegulatoryGuard AI

Setup, launch, and walkthrough guide for the IBM Bob 2.0 Hackathon MVP — pre-clinical compliance engine.

Contents
  1. Overview
  2. Installation & Setup
  3. Launching the Dashboard
  4. Dashboard Walkthrough
  5. Using Custom Rules
  6. Bob 2.0 Narrative Generation
  7. Exporting Results
  8. Running the Pipeline Standalone
  9. FAQ & Troubleshooting

1  Overview

RegulatoryGuard AI is a three-tier, flat-file pre-clinical data compliance engine built for the IBM Bob 2.0 Hackathon. It automates the detection of dosing variance deviations across animal cohorts, surfaces compliance verdicts in a modern Streamlit dashboard, and generates eCTD-ready narratives via the IBM Bob 2.0 large language model API.

Architecture at a glance

TierComponentRole
1 — RulesRegulatoryGuardAI_Rules_Example.csv → regulatory_rules.jsonScience-team-authored variance thresholds per assay parameter
2 — Engineprocess_data.pyPandas engine: computes deviation %, assigns traffic-light status, maps cohort → rule
3 — UI & AIapp.py + Bob 2.0 APIStreamlit dashboard + AI narrative generation

Traffic-light compliance verdicts

INCLUDE — deviation ≤ minor limit REVIEW — between minor & major limit EXCLUDE — exceeds major limit

Key capabilities

  • Multi-project workspace with unique 15-digit project IDs
  • Per-record 15-digit IDs (first 6 digits derived from the project ID)
  • Import delta detection — new records vs. previously seen records highlighted
  • Custom rules upload (CSV or JSON) overriding the default rulebook
  • Bob 2.0 AI narrative generation with graceful placeholder fallback
  • One-click eCTD-ready CSV export

2  Installation & Setup

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.10 or later
  • pip (comes with Python) or conda
  • Git (optional — you can also download the ZIP)
  • ~200 MB free disk space
Tip: Using a virtual environment is strongly recommended to avoid dependency conflicts with other projects.

Step-by-step

  • 1
    Clone or download the project 
    git clone https://github.com/your-org/RegulatoryGuardAI.git
cd RegulatoryGuardAI
  • 2
    Create and activate a virtual environment 
    # macOS / Linux
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

# Windows
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate
  • 3
    Install dependencies 
    pip install -r requirements.txt
    The following packages will be installed:
    • streamlit >= 1.35
    • pandas >= 2.0
    • numpy >= 1.26
    • requests >= 2.31
  • 4
    Compile the default rulebook (only needed once, or after editing the CSV) 
    python convert_rules_dynamic.py RegulatoryGuardAI_Rules_Example.csv
    This produces regulatory_rules.json at the project root.
Already done? A pre-compiled regulatory_rules.json is included in the repo — you can skip step 4 unless you modify the rules CSV.

3  Launching the Dashboard

From the project root (with the virtual environment active):

streamlit run app.py

Streamlit will print something like:

  You can now view your Streamlit app in your browser.
  Local URL:  http://localhost:8501
  Network URL: http://192.168.x.x:8501

Open http://localhost:8501 in your browser.

Port conflict? Use streamlit run app.py --server.port 8080 to run on a different port.

4  Dashboard Walkthrough

4.1 — Sidebar

The left sidebar is divided into four sections:

SectionPurpose
🗂 ProjectCreate a new project (name + description → unique 15-digit ID assigned automatically) or switch to an existing one.
📋 Compliance RulesDownload the template rules CSV; upload a custom rules file (CSV or JSON).
📂 DatasetLoad the built-in mock dataset or upload your own pre-clinical CSV.
🤖 Bob 2.0 NarrativeOptional endpoint URL and API key for AI narrative generation.

4.2 — Executive Summary

After running the compliance check, four KPI cards appear at the top of the main panel:

  • Total Records — number of rows analysed in this import, with new-record delta
  • ✓ Include — records within all acceptance limits (green)
  • ⚠ Review — records between minor and major variance limits (yellow)
  • ✕ Exclude — records exceeding the major variance limit (red)

4.3 — Distribution Charts

  • Status Distribution — bar chart of INCLUDE / REVIEW / EXCLUDE counts
  • Deviation % by Cohort — mean deviation per cohort group
  • Deviation % Histogram — frequency distribution across deviation buckets

4.4 — Interactive Data Viewer

Filter the results table by:

  • Status multi-select (INCLUDE / REVIEW / EXCLUDE)
  • Cohort multi-select
  • Free-text search across Animal ID and Notes fields

Each row includes: Record_ID, Animal_ID, Cohort, Target_Dose_mg_kg, Actual_Dose_mg_kg, Deviation_Pct, Status (badge), System_Action, Applied_Rule, and Delta (NEW / EXISTING).

4.5 — Import History

Expand the Import History panel at the bottom to see a timestamped log of all compliance runs within the current session, including import IDs and new-record counts.

Project IDs and Record IDs: Every project is assigned a random 15-digit numeric ID. Each imported record receives its own 15-digit ID where the first 6 digits match the last 6 digits of the project ID, enabling traceability across exports.

5  Using Custom Rules

Download the template

Click "⬇ Download Rules Template" in the sidebar to get RegulatoryGuardAI_Rules_Example.csv. Open it in any spreadsheet editor.

CSV column reference

ColumnTypeDescription
Assay_ParametertextName of the assay (must match cohort mapping)
UnittextUnit of measurement (for display only)
Minor_Variance_Limit_PercentnumberUpper boundary of the INCLUDE zone (%)
Major_Variance_Limit_PercentnumberUpper boundary of the REVIEW zone; beyond this = EXCLUDE (%)
Action_RequiredtextAction text shown in the REVIEW row (e.g. Review / Exclude)

Upload your rules

  • 1
    Edit the CSV template with your thresholds and save it.
  • 2
    In the sidebar under 📋 Compliance Rules, use the Upload custom rules file picker.
  • 3
    A success message confirms how many rules were loaded.
  • 4
    Click "▶ Run Compliance Check" — the engine will now use your rules.
You can also upload a JSON file (.json) that already follows the regulatory_rules.json schema — the app accepts both formats.

Cohort-to-rule mapping (default)

CohortAssay Parameter Applied
Group_1_LowBody Weight Change
Group_2_MidSerum Glucose
Group_3_HighHeart Rate
Group_4_ControlAlanine Aminotransferase (ALT)

Cohorts not in this mapping fall back to the rule with the most conservative (lowest) minor variance limit.

6  Bob 2.0 Narrative Generation

RegulatoryGuard AI integrates the IBM Bob 2.0 large language model to automatically produce an eCTD Section 2.6-style compliance narrative from the processed compliance summary.

Configuration

  • 1
    In the sidebar under 🤖 Bob 2.0 Narrative, enter your Endpoint URL (e.g. https://us-south.ml.cloud.ibm.com/ml/v1/text/generation).
  • 2
    Enter your API Key (it is masked as a password field and never stored).
  • 3
    After running the compliance check, click "🤖 Generate Narrative".
No credentials? If either field is left blank, the app will display a clearly labelled placeholder narrative — the rest of the dashboard remains fully functional.

What the narrative includes

  • Total number of records analysed
  • Per-status counts and percentages
  • Maximum deviation observed and which cohort it occurred in
  • Which assay rules were applied
  • A professional summary sentence suitable for submission

API call details

Method: POST

Headers: Authorization: Bearer <api_key>, Content-Type: application/json

Model: ibm/granite-13b-instruct-v2 (default)

No extra SDK — called via standard requests library.

7  Exporting Results

Click "⬇ Export eCTD Package (CSV)" (below the data table) to download the full processed dataset as a CSV file named audit_ready_report_<project_id>.csv.

Exported columns

ColumnDescription
Record_ID15-digit unique record identifier (first 6 = last 6 of project ID)
Import_TSUTC timestamp of the import run
Animal_IDOriginal animal identifier from the source data
CohortDose group assignment
Target_Dose_mg_kgIntended dose (mg/kg)
Actual_Dose_mg_kgAdministered dose (mg/kg)
Deviation_PctAbsolute deviation % from target
StatusINCLUDE / REVIEW / EXCLUDE
System_ActionRecommended action text
Applied_RuleName of the assay rule applied to this record
DeltaNEW (first import) or EXISTING (seen in a prior import)
The CSV is ready for direct attachment to an eCTD submission package or import into a LIMS / EDC system.

8  Running the Pipeline Standalone

Each tier can be run independently from the command line — useful for batch processing, CI pipelines, or quick testing without opening the dashboard.

Tier 1 — Compile rules

python convert_rules_dynamic.py RegulatoryGuardAI_Rules_Example.csv
# Output: regulatory_rules.json

# Custom output path:
python convert_rules_dynamic.py my_rules.csv my_output.json

Tier 2 — Run compliance engine

python process_data.py
# Reads:  RegulatoryGuardAI_Test_Records/RegulatoryGuardAI_mock_preclinical_data.csv
#         regulatory_rules.json
# Output: audit_ready_report.csv
Expected distribution for the mock dataset: ~90% INCLUDE, ~7% REVIEW, ~3% EXCLUDE across 3,200 records.

Full pipeline (one-liner)

python convert_rules_dynamic.py RegulatoryGuardAI_Rules_Example.csv && python process_data.py

9  FAQ & Troubleshooting

The dashboard shows "No active project" after I create one

The project is stored in the Streamlit session state. If the page fully reloads (e.g. after a code change while the dev server is running), session state is cleared. Simply re-create the project in the sidebar — this is expected behaviour for the MVP's in-memory persistence.

Clicking "Load Mock Dataset" does nothing

Ensure the file RegulatoryGuardAI_Test_Records/RegulatoryGuardAI_mock_preclinical_data.csv exists relative to the directory you launched Streamlit from. Always run streamlit run app.py from the project root.

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'streamlit'

Your virtual environment is not active, or you forgot to run pip install -r requirements.txt. Re-activate the environment (source .venv/bin/activate) and reinstall.

Rules uploaded but compliance check still uses old thresholds

After uploading new rules, click "▶ Run Compliance Check" again. Uploading the file updates the rules in session state; the engine only uses them on the next run.

Bob 2.0 returns an error or empty text

  • Verify the endpoint URL is correct and includes the full path (e.g. /v1/text/generation).
  • Confirm the API key is valid and has not expired.
  • Check that your network allows outbound HTTPS to the IBM Cloud endpoint.
  • If the issue persists, the placeholder narrative is used automatically — the app remains fully functional.

How do I add my own cohort-to-rule mappings?

Open app.py and find the COHORT_RULE_MAP dictionary near the top. Add entries in the format "Your_Cohort_Name": "Assay_Parameter_Name". The assay parameter name must exactly match the Assay_Parameter column value in your rules CSV.

I want to persist projects across sessions

The MVP uses Streamlit session state (in-memory). For persistence, export the results CSV after each session. A database backend is out of scope for this hackathon release.

Port 8501 is already in use

streamlit run app.py --server.port 8080

Python version compatibility

RegulatoryGuard AI requires Python 3.10 or later. Run python --version to verify. On macOS / Linux you may need to use python3 instead of python.

9  FAQ & Troubleshooting

The dashboard shows "No active project" after I create one

The project is stored in the Streamlit session state. If the page fully reloads (e.g. after a code change while the dev server is running), session state is cleared. Simply re-create the project in the sidebar — this is expected behaviour for the MVP's in-memory persistence.

Clicking "Load Mock Dataset" does nothing

Ensure the file RegulatoryGuardAI_Test_Records/RegulatoryGuardAI_mock_preclinical_data.csv exists relative to the directory you launched Streamlit from. Always run streamlit run app.py from the project root.

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'streamlit'

Your virtual environment is not active, or you forgot to run pip install -r requirements.txt. Re-activate the environment (source .venv/bin/activate) and reinstall.

Rules uploaded but compliance check still uses old thresholds

After uploading new rules, click "▶ Run Compliance Check" again. Uploading the file updates the rules in session state; the engine only uses them on the next run.

watsonx.ai narrative returns an error or empty text

  • Check that WATSONX_PROJECT_ID and WATSONX_API_KEY in .env are correct (no extra spaces or quotes).
  • Confirm the API key is valid and has not been deleted — regenerate it at cloud.ibm.com/iam/apikeys if needed.
  • Verify the project ID matches the one shown in your watsonx.ai project under Manage → General.
  • Check that your network allows outbound HTTPS to iam.cloud.ibm.com and us-south.ml.cloud.ibm.com.
  • If the issue persists, the placeholder narrative is used automatically — the app remains fully functional.

How do I add my own cohort-to-rule mappings?

Open app.py and find the COHORT_RULE_MAP dictionary near the top. Add entries in the format "Your_Cohort_Name": "Assay_Parameter_Name". The assay parameter name must exactly match the Assay_Parameter column value in your rules CSV.

I want to persist projects across sessions

The MVP uses Streamlit session state (in-memory). For persistence, export the results CSV after each session. A database backend is out of scope for this hackathon release.

Port 8501 is already in use

streamlit run app.py --server.port 8080

Python version compatibility

RegulatoryGuard AI requires Python 3.10 or later. Run python --version to verify. On macOS / Linux you may need to use python3 instead of python.
